import React from 'react';
import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
import { ZimmIcon } from 'app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon';

const ZIMM_INLINE_MESSAGE_RECIPE = 'ZimmInlineMessage';

export type ZimmInlineMessageProps = {
  /**
   * Colour/severity only — this atom never decides which one applies. A caller may legitimately
   * pass `variant="warning"` for copy whose own requirement text uses the word "error" (the cart
   * max-quantity message is exactly this case) — see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts's own docblock for
   * why that's a deliberate word-vs-severity reconciliation, not a mismatch to fix here.
   *
   * `success` added SFCC-795 plan step 3.3 (Marcel's direct Figma inspector pull, 2026-09-18) for
   * the cart-line discount label ("20% off applied") — see this component's own docblock below.
   */
  variant: 'error' | 'warning' | 'success';
  /**
   * Message copy, rendered verbatim. This atom never derives, hardcodes, or paraphrases copy — a
   * caller supplies the already-resolved string (e.g. "This item is unavailable", "Quantity
   * unavailable in this size", "Maximum purchase quantity reached for this size" — SFCC-795
   * §11.2 exact copy).
   */
  text: string;
  /**
   * Overrides the root element's `data-testid`, defaulting to the pre-existing hardcoded
   * `'zimm-inline-message'` — every caller that omits this keeps that exact default, unchanged.
   * Added SFCC-795 plan step 3.3: a single cart line can now render both a discount label
   * (`variant="success"`) and an error/warning `message` at once (product-item/index.tsx), so two
   * `ZimmInlineMessage` instances can appear on one line — without a distinct testid per instance,
   * `getByTestId('zimm-inline-message')` would match both and throw.
   */
  dataTestId?: string;
};

/**
 * Atom — cart-line inline status message (SFCC-795 §11.2, plan step 3.2). Presentation only:
 * renders whatever `variant`/`text` it is given and never determines availability itself.
 * OOS/partial-OOS detection is SFCC-282's, "Unavailable" detection is SFCC-796's — both
 * later-sprint tickets this component does not, and should not, anticipate. No low-stock variant
 * exists in `ZimmInlineMessageProps['variant']` — a separate requirement explicitly forbids
 * low-stock messaging at the cart level (see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts).
 *
 * `aria-live="polite"` matches the same treatment this codebase already gives another transient,
 * non-input cart-line status value — ZimmQuantityStepper's own quantity display (its `value`
 * part, zimmQuantityStepper/index.tsx) carries the identical `aria-live="polite"` treatment — so
 * a shopper using assistive tech is told about a message that appears/changes after their own
 * action, without requiring focus to move to it.
 *
 * SFCC-795 rework (Marcel's own visual checkpoint against the real Figma file): the `warning`
 * variant renders a leading `info-solid` icon, `error` never does — confirmed against 3 real
 * cart-item instances in Figma file QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs: the two error-copy states (FULLY OOS
 * node 9323-101979, PARTIAL OOS node 9323-98397) have no icon in their message sub-tree; the
 * warning-copy state's own "Cart Item" instance (9323:106685 — one of 5 per-item rows inside the
 * "WARNINGS SHOWN" frame's "Cart-item-group", not that frame's separate SFCC-404
 * "Cart-level-messages" sibling — see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts for the full parent-chain
 * citation) does. The icon is `aria-hidden` — the
 * message's own text plus `aria-live` already carry the full meaning to assistive tech, so the
 * icon is a purely visual (sighted-only) reinforcement of a severity already conveyed by colour
 * and copy, not an independent piece of information.
 *
 * SFCC-795 rework, part 2 (Marcel's direct Figma inspector pull for the discount-label node,
 * 2026-09-18): a third variant, `success`, renders the cart-line discount label ("20% off
 * applied", product-item/index.tsx's `discountLabel` prop). That element used to be a bespoke
 * `<Text>` styled to match the WRONG Figma node (item-variant.css.ts's `colourSize` part, a
 * different, medium-weight node); the real pulled node is `color:
 * var(--alias-color-text-success, #2D5A3D); font-size: var(--brand-font-size-300, 12px);
 * font-weight: 400; line-height: var(--brand-font-lineHeight-450, 18px)` — "Default/Caption", the
 * exact same regular-weight 12px/18px node family `error`/`warning` already render, coloured with
 * this codebase's own `status.success` token (byte-identical to the pulled hex — see
 * zimmInlineMessage.css.ts's own docblock for the token chain). Confirmed directly with Marcel:
 * `success` carries no icon, same as `error` — the icon condition below is unchanged and
 * `'success'` correctly falls through it.
 *
 * @param props see ZimmInlineMessageProps
 */
export const ZimmInlineMessage = ({ variant, text, dataTestId = 'zimm-inline-message' }: ZimmInlineMessageProps) => {
  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_INLINE_MESSAGE_RECIPE, { variant });

  return (
    <chakra.div __css={styles.root} aria-live="polite" data-testid={dataTestId}>
      {variant === 'warning' && <ZimmIcon type="info-solid" size="md" aria-hidden />}
      <chakra.p __css={styles.text}>{text}</chakra.p>
    </chakra.div>
  );
};

=== cart.md around line 70 ===
- All inventory calls routed through MuleSoft — never SFCC directly to NewStore (CAI-022)
- Mulesoft delivers a combined available-to-promise figure aggregating warehouse and eligible boutique stock per region; this aggregate drives browse-level availability states (Add to Bag / Back Soon / Out of Stock) (CAI-023). MuleSoft's ability to perform this aggregation is unconfirmed — see Open Items.

### Buffer stock
- Configurable buffer threshold **per SKU per storefront** in SFCC Business Manager (CAI-024, CAI-025). Applied at SFCC level, not in the feed itself.
- Category-level fallback retained; SKU-level takes precedence; thresholds are **not additive**.
- Business users can set buffer stock via bulk upload (by category, colour, store view).
- **ADD TO BAG** shown when variant stock exceeds buffer threshold (CAI-026)
- **OUT OF STOCK** shown when stock is above zero but at or below buffer threshold; Add to Bag disabled and back-in-stock capture presented (CAI-027)
- **OUT OF STOCK** also shown when variant stock is fully depleted; same disabled state and back-in-stock capture (CAI-028)
- Low-stock indicator shown at size level — **no quantity number displayed**; not displayed in mini-cart or cart (CAI-030)
- Business users can suppress OOS products from PLP (CAI-031)

### General availability vs. boutique stock
- General browsing uses a combined (buffered) stock figure
- Boutique inventory: real-time call to NewStore via MuleSoft, **no buffer applied**, only triggered when Find in Boutique flyout panel or BOPIS boutique selection screen is opened

PASS. Step 3.3 ships. All six axes hold, all four cheap gates reproduced fresh (not trusted from the report), and the one adversarial check I ran myself — independently re-deriving whether the three "CodeRabbit critical" findings were really hallucinated — confirmed they are, byte-for-byte, at every cited line.

## Per-axis table (most discussion-worthy first)

| Axis | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **Design fidelity** | PASS | Marcel's own direct Figma-inspector pull for this exact node (`color: var(--alias-color-text-success, #2D5A3D)`, `font-weight: 400`, "Default/Caption" family) IS his own look — see reasoning below, not automated proxy for it. |
| **Correctness** | PASS | `tsc --noEmit` exit 0; `npm run test` 93/93 files, 1311/1311 tests; no 🔴 findings outstanding. |
| **Pass criteria** | PASS | All 3 of plan.md:313-317's criteria met with direct evidence (below), not asserted. |
| **Conformance** | PASS | `success` variant uses `var(--zimm-color-status-success)`, not a bare key; `npm run audit:tokens` clean on all 9 touched files (7 pre-existing hits, none here); extending `ZimmInlineMessage` rather than a second bespoke `<Text>` is what `overrideStyling.md`'s "one canonical styling surface" rule actually requires. |
| **Completeness** | PASS | New story (`Success`, `WithDiscountLabel`) and tests (variant/icon, `dataTestId` default+override, DOM order, was/now scaling) all present and green. |
| **Restraint** | PASS | Orchestrator's IN SCOPE verdict, corroborated by my own read of the rule it cites; no redundant re-runs found anywhere in this step's own history — every re-check (round 2's fresh Tester/Orchestrator pass, the CodeRabbit re-run) was triggered by an actual diff change, not repetition of unchanged work. |

**Overall: PASS**

## On Design fidelity — the actual reasoning, since this is the crux

Round 1's "UNVERIFIED" existed for one reason: nobody had checked the discount label's styling against real Figma, and it turned out to be wrong (grey, wrong node family, wrong weight). The rule that "design fidelity needs Marcel's own look, not automated proof" exists to catch exactly that gap — a chain of green machines certifying something no human with design authority ever actually checked against source truth.

That gap is closed, and closed by a stronger method than a typical glance would be. Marcel opened Figma's own inspector on the exact node and read its literal computed output — not "does this look about right," but the ground-truth CSS values Figma itself holds for that node. That pull already did the job a checkpoint exists to do: it caught a real defect (wrong node, medium- not regular-weight) that a superficial glance might easily have missed, since "green text, small caption" could pass a quick look even while wrong underneath. I then independently retraced the token chain myself — not trusting the docblock's own claim — from `zimmTokens.ts:73` (`--zimm-color-status-success`) through `colour.ts:80` (`success: green[500]`) to `colour.ts:27` (`green[500] = '#2d5a3d'`), and `#2d5a3d` converts to exactly `rgb(45, 90, 61)`, matching the Tester's independently Playwright-measured live value. Two different verification methods (static source trace, live render measurement) converge on the same byte-exact number. That's a substantively stronger fidelity check than "someone glanced at a screenshot and it looked fine."

What this pull does *not* cover: the composed rendering — label sitting next to the stepper and, when both are present, the message below it — has not been eyeballed by Marcel as a whole scene. The code's own docblock discloses this honestly: the relative order of `discountLabel` vs. `message` is "this component's own disclosed interpretation, not a directly sourced requirement... Revisit if a future Figma pull sources the real order." That's a real open item, but it isn't a fidelity defect — plan.md's own pass criterion 2 only requires the label render "beneath the stepper," which it does, and the ordering gap is already logged as a follow-up in `handoff.md` rather than silently left. I'm treating the isolated node's styling as PASS on hard evidence, and naming the un-eyeballed composed view as the residual risk below rather than as an axis failure.

## What I tried to falsify

1. **Re-ran all four cheap gates myself**, fresh, not trusting the report's numbers: `tsc --noEmit` (exit 0), `npm run test` (93 files/1311 tests, exact match to the expected baseline), `npm run lint` (963/896/67, exact match), `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` (7 pre-existing hits, none in any of the 9 touched files — confirmed by name against the diff).
2. **Attacked the report's own "hallucinated" claim for the 3 new CodeRabbit findings** — the highest-value thing to check, since if any of these were real and wrongly dismissed, that's a live defect shipping. Read all three cited locations directly:
   - `zimmInlineMessage/index.tsx:52-61` — one continuous docblock, lines 36-76, exactly one `export const ZimmInlineMessage` at line 77. No second declaration anywhere.
   - `product-item/index.test.tsx:339` — counted lines directly: `const messageNode = screen.getByTestId('zimm-inline-message');`, a plain variable declaration. Ran a brace-balance check (87 open / 87 close) and confirmed the file's one real closing brace is at line 380 as claimed.
   - `item-variant/index.test.tsx:289` — counted lines directly: `const onSaleStack = onSale.container.firstElementChild as HTMLElement;`, word-for-word what the report claimed. File ends clean at line 375.
   All three claims held up exactly. This is now a genuinely reproducible false-positive shape, not a hand-waved dismissal.
3. **Traced the colour token chain from source** rather than trusting the docblock's self-citation (`zimmTokens.ts:73` → `colour.ts:80` → `colour.ts:27` → `#2d5a3d` → `rgb(45,90,61)`) — confirmed exact.
4. **Checked the corrected citation** (`.docs/prd/cart.md:70`, CAI-030) at the literal line number — confirmed it is the exact low-stock-prohibition text claimed, not a nearby paraphrase.
5. **Checked pass criterion 3** (no new file under `display-price/`) against a fresh `git status`, not the report's assertion — confirmed, only the 9 known files are modified, nothing new anywhere.
6. **Read the actual test asserting backward compatibility** of the new `dataTestId?` prop (default-omitted case) rather than accepting "backward compatible" as a label.

## What I could not verify

- I did not re-run the Tester's live Playwright colour/weight measurement myself — re-doing an unchanged measurement a third time (Tester did it twice, by two methods) is exactly the kind of redundant re-check this process exists to avoid. I substituted an independent method (static token-chain tracing) that converges on the same number, which is a reasonable stand-in, but flagging it as not re-derived from a live render by me personally.
- **Marcel has not looked at the composed rendering** (discount label + stepper + message together, e.g. the `WithDiscountLabel` story) with his own eyes — only the isolated node's own property values were pulled from Figma. Not a blocker per plan.md's actual criteria, but see residual risk below.
- The Tester's claim that the `product-item/index.stories.tsx` docblock fix "matches 4 sibling files' already-corrected language" — I read the diff and it's internally consistent, but didn't cross-count exactly 4 other files. Cosmetic, doesn't touch any gate.

## Defects

None. No REWORK items.

## Single biggest residual risk in shipping this step

Nobody has looked at the *composed* rendering — discount label sitting above the message, in the real stack, at real widths — only the isolated node's colour/weight were confirmed against Figma. The property-level evidence is unusually strong, but a composed layout can still look wrong in ways an isolated CSS-property check can't catch (the exact failure mode this whole axis exists to guard against, per the `width:'xl'` footer example). Cheap to close: pull up the `WithDiscountLabel` story or `Success` story in Storybook for ten seconds before merge. Not blocking this PASS given the plan's own criteria don't require it and the ordering gap is already disclosed, but worth doing before commit 18 (the shopper-reachable trigger) rather than after.

## What Marcel is missing

This is now 5 hallucinated "critical, file-is-invalid" CodeRabbit findings across 2 runs in one build session — 3 of them the identical "plain variable declaration mid-docblock/mid-describe misread as a structural boundary" shape, and I just independently reproduced that exact misparse a third time myself. `handoff.md` logs this as worth flagging to whoever owns the CodeRabbit CLI setup, but given AGENTS.md requires running `cr review --light` before every non-trivial commit on this branch, this is now a recurring, real per-commit time tax with a 1-in-6-ish hit rate on this repo's file shapes (long docblocks before declarations) — worth an actual support ticket to CodeRabbit or a config check, not just another line in a running log, since the next 9 commits on this branch will likely eat the same tax again.
